# Store variables and resolve them along the scope chain

## Intent

A workspace runs with configuration that people set at three levels: a user, an organization and the workspace itself. Parley keeps readable named values, variables, at each of those levels and answers one question in one place: which value does a given workspace or task fork run with, and where did it come from. The same chain decides which stored secret a sandbox receives under a name, with one rule that must never bend: a fork owned by someone who cannot write to the parent never receives the parent's secrets. Putting the chain in one component means every caller, every route and every sandbox gets the same answer.

## Goals

- A user, an organization member and a workspace owner create, list, update and delete variables in the `user`, `org` and `workspace` scopes over twelve REST routes, with values readable in every answer.
- Keys are unique per scope ignoring case, at most 255 characters; values are at most 262,144 bytes; a scope holds at most 100 variables; a create is all-or-nothing.
- `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved` answers the variables a workspace or fork runs with, merged along the chain workspace → parent → org → user, each entry with its `origin`.
- One resolution function gives sandboxes the secret stored under each of a list of names for a workspace or fork, skipping the parent's scope when the fork's owner has no write access to the parent, and skipping reserved names in the parent's scope for everyone.
- Every created entry, update and delete writes one hub event without the value; a failed request writes none.
- A workspace's variables go when the workspace or fork is removed, in the same transaction; a workspace created again under the same slug starts empty.
- `parley vars create|list|update|delete|resolve` drive the routes from the shell, including a create that writes to several scopes in one command.

- The encrypted secret store, encryption keys and rotation, the secret routes `/user/secrets`, `/orgs/:slug/secrets`, `/workspaces/:slug/secrets`, the events `parley.secret.*`, the `503 secrets_unavailable` answer, removal of secrets and `parley secrets …`: package 39 `secrets`. This package reads secrets through that store and never writes one.

This package delivers the function they call.

This package declares its user and org routes as naming no workspace and its workspace routes as naming `:slug`, and adds nothing to the guard.

## Requirements

All paths are relative to `/api/v1`. Every route obeys the platform conventions (PLAT-FR-010 to PLAT-FR-019): the error envelope `{"error":{"code","message","error_type"}}`, the check order (authentication, binding guard, PAT scope, scope access, request validation, state, act), list paging and idempotency keys. They are not restated per route.

### Variable entries and limits

A variable belongs to one owner: a scope (`user`, `org` or `workspace`) and a scope id (the user id, the organization id, or the workspace slug). A task fork is a workspace and has its own `workspace` scope. An entry has a `key`, a `value`, `created_at` and `updated_at`. Responses carry `{key, value, created_at, updated_at}` and never the owner, which the route states. Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC with whole seconds.

| Rule | Value |
|---|---|
| Key characters | ASCII letters, digits and `_`; the first character is not a digit |
| Key length | 1 to 255 |
| Key matching | case-insensitive for uniqueness, update, delete and resolution; the key is stored and returned with the casing given at create |
| Value size | at most 262,144 bytes, counted in bytes; the empty string is allowed |
| Entries per scope | at most 100 variables per scope and scope id; secrets are counted apart |

Variable values are not encrypted. Every variable route keeps working when no secret encryption key is configured (SEC-FR-011).

### Who may use which scope

SEC-FR-001: a PAT needs `vars:read` or `vars:write` for a read (the lists and the resolved route) and `vars:write` for a write (create, update, delete); otherwise `403 insufficient_scope`. API keys and the admin token are not scope-checked.

| Scope | Routes under | Who | Refusal |
|---|---|---|---|
| `user` | `/user/vars` | any credential with a user; the scope id is the caller's user id | the admin token gets `403 forbidden` with the message `user-scoped endpoints require a user credential` (SEC-FR-004) |
| `org` | `/orgs/:slug/vars` | members of the organization, and the admin token; `:slug` is the organization's slug or its UUID, as on the secret routes | an unknown organization and a caller who is not a member get `404 not_found` with the same body (SEC-FR-005) |
| `workspace` | `/workspaces/:slug/vars` | SEC-FR-006: the owner and the admin token read and write; an org member reads (list, resolved) | a member's write gets `403 forbidden` with the message `org members have read-only access to this workspace`; anyone else, and an unknown slug, get `404 not_found` with the message `workspace not found` |

The workspace's status (for example `archived`) does not matter, and an exclusive maintenance operation does not block these routes (SEC-FR-006).

### Creating variables

`POST /user/vars`, `POST /orgs/:slug/vars`, `POST /workspaces/:slug/vars` (SEC-FR-007). The body is `{"entries":[{"key": string, "value": string}, …]}`; a missing `value` is the empty string. The route accepts `Idempotency-Key`. The answer is `201` with `{"items":[{key, value, created_at, updated_at}, …]}` in request order; every entry has the same `created_at`, equal to its `updated_at`.

The create is all-or-nothing. Checks run in this order and the first failure decides:

1. `entries` is a non-empty array: else `400 invalid_request`.
2. Each key is valid: else `400 invalid_request`, the message names the key.
3. Each value is a string within the size limit: else `400 invalid_request`, the message names the key.
4. No two keys of the request are equal ignoring case: else `400 invalid_request`, the message names the key.
5. The scope's count plus the new entries is at most 100: else `429` with `error_type` `secret_limit_reached` and the message `maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded`. The route is specified "as `POST /user/secrets`", so variables use the same `error_type`. A full scope answers this even when a key of the request also conflicts (§11.10).
6. No key is already present ignoring case: else `409 conflict` with the message `key "<k>" already exists`.

Of two concurrent creates of the same key in one scope, exactly one answers `201` and the other `409 conflict`.

### Listing, updating and deleting

- `GET /user/vars`, `GET /orgs/:slug/vars`, `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars` answer `200` with `{"items":[…],"next_cursor":…}`, ordered by key ascending ignoring case, with `limit` and `cursor` as on every list (SEC-FR-010). A workspace's list holds only that workspace's own variables, never a parent's.
- `PATCH …/vars/:key` takes `{"value": string}` (SEC-FR-008). An absent or `null` value, a value that is not a string and a value over the size limit are `400 invalid_request`; `""` is valid. The key is matched ignoring case; no match is `404 not_found` with the message `key "<k>" not found`. The stored key casing and `created_at` are kept; `updated_at` becomes now. The answer is `200` with the entry.
- `DELETE …/vars/:key` matches the key ignoring case (SEC-FR-009). No match is `404 not_found` with the same message. Success is `204` with no body.
- `resolved` is reserved under `/workspaces/:slug/vars/` (SEC-FR-017): `PATCH` and `DELETE` on `/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved` answer `405 method_not_allowed`. No route reads a single entry by key: `GET` on a `…/vars/:key` path answers `405 method_not_allowed`.

### Events

SEC-FR-016 and §11.8. Each created entry writes one `parley.variable.create`, each update one `parley.variable.update`, each delete one `parley.variable.delete`, in the same transaction as the change. `resource_type` is `variable`, `action` is `create`, `update` or `delete`, `resource_id` is the stored key, and `metadata` is `{"scope": "user"|"org"|"workspace", "scope_id": <user id, org id or workspace slug>, "key": <stored key>}`. The event's `workspace` field is the slug for the workspace scope and null otherwise. No event carries a value. A failed request writes none. If the event cannot be written the change is not made and the answer is `500 internal`.

### The resolution chain

§11.3. The chain of a workspace W, highest priority first:

| Step | Scope | `origin` | Included when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | W's `workspace` scope | `workspace` | always |
| 2 | the parent's `workspace` scope | `parent` | W is a task fork |
| 3 | the `org` scope of W's organization | `org` | W has an organization and W's owner is currently a member of it |
| 4 | the `user` scope of W's owner | `user` | always |

The user is always the workspace's owner, never the caller. For a fork, the owner is whoever created the fork and the organization is the parent's. The chain is the same for every caller, the admin token included, and is worked out again at every resolution, so a change of membership or ownership applies to the next one.

### Resolved variables

`GET /workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved` (SEC-FR-015) needs only variable read access on `:slug`: the owner, the admin token or an org member, and for a PAT `vars:read` or `vars:write`. It needs no access to any other scope of the chain: resolution is use, not read access. It answers `200` with a list `{"items":[{key, value, origin, created_at, updated_at}, …],"next_cursor":…}` ordered by key ascending ignoring case.

Variables resolve by merge: for each key, compared ignoring case, the entry of the highest-priority scope that has it wins entirely, with its key casing, value, timestamps and `origin`. A fork's resolved set includes the parent's variables with `origin` `parent`. A fork's variable of the same name as its parent's wins; deleting the fork's entry shows the parent's again (§11.10). When a fork's owner has left the organization, the fork's chain has no org step, and the parent step stays for the callers who can still reach the fork (§11.10).

### Secrets by name along the chain

Sandboxes resolve secrets by name, for credentials and for exposed secrets (§11.3, SBX-FR-024, SBX-FR-065). This package delivers the one function they call: given a workspace slug and a list of names, it answers, for each name, the value of the first scope in the chain that has the name (compared ignoring case) and that scope's `origin`, or that the name is missing, together with the scopes that were searched in order. Two rules narrow step 2 for secrets:

- Step 2 applies only when the fork's owner has write access to the parent workspace, which only the parent's owner has. The test is on the fork's owner, never on the caller. In a fork owned by a read-only org member the parent's secrets are never read.
- Reserved names (`GIT_PAT`, `GIT_USERNAME`, `GIT_PASSWORD`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_PAT`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_USERNAME`, `UPSTREAM_GIT_PASSWORD`, `FORGE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, compared ignoring case) are skipped in step 2 for everyone.

Values are read at every call and never cached: a rotated secret is answered by the next call, and a fork owner who loses write access to the parent loses step 2 at the next call (§11.10). A secret that is found and cannot be read or decrypted fails the whole call with an error that names the key and the scope and never a value; it is never treated as missing and never replaced by a lower scope's value (SEC-FR-013).

### Removal with the owner

SEC-FR-014. Deleting a workspace deletes its variables in the same transaction; this includes the deletion and the expiry of a task fork. When that transaction is rolled back the variables are still there. A workspace created again under the same slug starts with no variables. No variable event is written for a removal. Deleting a user or an organization deletes that scope's variables in the transaction of the deletion; when the deletion is refused or rolled back the variables are still there.

### `parley vars`

§11.6. The commands follow the CLI conventions (PLAT-FR-090 to PLAT-FR-095).

- **Scope flags** `--user`, `--org <slug>`, `--workspace <slug>`. Without a flag the scope is the user. `list`, `update` and `delete` accept at most one; more is a usage error (exit 2).
- `parley vars create <KEY=VALUE[,KEY=VALUE…]>… | <KEY> --from-stdin` calls `POST /<scope>/vars` once for each scope flag, in the order user → org → workspace, and prints one document `{"results":[{"scope":"user"|"org"|"workspace","items":[…]}, …]}` holding the scopes that succeeded. A failing scope does not stop the others; each failed scope's error envelope is printed once on stderr and the command exits 1 if any scope failed.
- **Values.** `KEY=VALUE` is split at the first `=`, so a value may contain `=`. A comma separates entries. `--from-stdin` takes one bare `KEY` and reads the value from standard input, dropping one trailing line ending.
- `parley vars list` calls `GET /<scope>/vars` and prints the entries of all pages as one document `{"items":[…]}`, as `parley secrets list` does.
- `parley vars update <KEY=VALUE> | <KEY> --from-stdin` calls `PATCH /<scope>/vars/<KEY>` and prints the entry.
- `parley vars delete <KEY>` calls `DELETE /<scope>/vars/<KEY>` and prints `{"deleted":"<KEY>"}`.
- `parley vars resolve <workspace-slug>` calls `GET /workspaces/<slug>/vars/resolved`, takes no scope flag and prints the resolved entries with `origin`.
- Key naming rules are checked by the hub. Malformed arguments are usage errors (exit 2) and nothing is sent.

### End-to-end flows

1. **A developer sets values at two levels and reads what the workspace runs with.** The developer, a member of an organization and owner of a workspace in it, posts `LOG_LEVEL=info` to `/orgs/:slug/vars` and `log_level=debug` to `/workspaces/:slug/vars`. `parleyd` stores both and writes one `parley.variable.create` for each. The developer reads `/workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved`; `parleyd` answers one entry, key `log_level`, value `debug`, `origin` `workspace`. The developer deletes the workspace's entry and reads again; the entry is now `LOG_LEVEL`, `info`, `origin` `org`.
2. **An org member's fork runs with the parent's variables and without its secrets.** A developer owns a workspace that holds a variable `REGION` and a secret `DEPLOY_KEY`. An org member owns a task fork of it. The org member reads the fork's resolved variables; `parleyd` answers `REGION` with `origin` `parent`. `parleyd` resolves the secret `DEPLOY_KEY` for the fork and for a fork the developer owns: it is missing for the member's fork, with the parent's scope absent from the scopes searched, and found with `origin` `parent` for the developer's fork.
3. **A developer manages variables from the shell.** The developer runs `parley vars create A=1,B=x=y --user --workspace <slug>`; the parley CLI sends one create to `/user/vars` and one to `/workspaces/<slug>/vars`; `parleyd` stores the entries; the CLI prints both scopes' results and exits 0. The developer runs `parley vars resolve <slug>`; the CLI prints `A` and `B` with `origin` `workspace`.

## Design Decisions

1. **Profile: full**, with three execution paths.
2. **Go; SQLite through `modernc.org/sqlite` behind `internal/store`; `net/http` with its method-and-pattern router; `github.com/spf13/cobra` for the CLI; the standard `testing` package with table-driven tests and `net/http/httptest`** (project decisions 1 to 4 and 7). The variable table is created by a schema migration this package registers with `internal/store`.
3. **Variables live in a table of their own**, keyed by scope, scope id and the lower-cased key, beside the stored casing. Why: the two collections have the same shape but different rules for values, and uniqueness ignoring case is then enforced by the store even under concurrent creates.
4. **`secret_limit_reached` for a full variable scope.** The source PRD specifies `POST /user/vars` "as `POST /user/secrets`" and defines no variable-specific type.
5. **Membership means membership of an `active` organization**, on the org routes and in step 3 of the chain. This package asks the same question the access rule asks of identity: the ids of the active organizations a user is a member of. A member of a blocked organization therefore gets `404 not_found` on that organization's variable routes, and a workspace of a blocked organization resolves without the org step. The admin token reaches a blocked organization's variables. The PRD says only "currently a member".
6. **The organization in the path** is resolved with the organization selector of package 05 (`internal/identity`): a value in UUID form is an id, any other value a slug. This is what the secret routes of package 39 do, and the PRD specifies the variable routes "as the secret routes". The scope resolvers of the three scopes (the admin-token refusal on `/user/…`, the one `404` body for an unknown organization, a non-member and a member of a blocked organization) answer exactly as package 39's do; only the workspace need differs (`read` and `write` here, `owner` there).
7. **Body members of the wrong type are `400 invalid_request`**: `entries` that is not an array, an entry that is not an object, a `key` that is absent or not a string, a `value` that is not a string. The PRD names only the missing and the oversized cases.
8. **Update validates before it looks the key up**, as the platform's check order puts request validation before state: an invalid body on an unknown key is `400`.
9. **A key `resolved` can be created like any other valid key.** The PRD blocks no name. In a workspace scope only the exact path segment `resolved` is reserved; such a key is still addressed by another casing (`…/vars/RESOLVED`), because keys match ignoring case and the router matches the literal segment exactly.
10. **The resolved list is paged like every list** (`limit`, `cursor`, default 50), merged from one consistent read of the store on every request.
11. **A missing record ends a step, not the resolution.** A fork whose parent record is missing has no parent step; a workspace whose owner no longer exists has no user step; a workspace whose organization no longer exists has no org step. Why: the PRD is silent, and leaving a scope out can never hand a caller a value it should not get.
12. **A secret with an empty value counts as present** in name resolution. "An empty `GIT_PAT` counts as no credential" is a rule of credential resolution (package 10), not of the chain.
13. **A name asked for twice is answered once**, and names are answered in the order first asked. An empty list of names is answered with no entries and no error.
14. **The secret store is read through package 39's `Get(scope, scope id, name)`**, which answers `(value, found, error)`, matches the name ignoring ASCII case, reads the store on every call and returns an error matching `ErrUnreadable` for an entry that cannot be decrypted. The resolution takes that one method as its reader, so tests can wrap it to record reads; it defines no second read operation.
15. **Removal with a workspace or a fork.** `internal/workspace` imports `internal/secret` (package 10 stores credentials as secrets), so `internal/secret` cannot import the registries of packages 14 and 16; the registration is written in `internal/hub`. This package exports `RemoveWorkspaceVars(tx, slug)`, which deletes every variable of that workspace scope inside the transaction it is given, writes no event and returns the store's error. Package 14's delete runs it as a remover of owned data (a function of the transaction and one slug that returns the ids of the tokens it revoked; this one returns none), and package 16's fork removal runs it as a removal participant (a function of the transaction, the fork's slug and the cause; the cause is not looked at). Packages 14 and 16 are dependencies of this package for that reason, and this package's task writes both registrations. (Package 39 exports `RemoveWorkspace` in the same form; it cannot depend on 14, so package 14 registers that one, and package 16 removes a fork's secrets directly.)
16. **Variables of a deleted user or organization are removed in the deletion's transaction**, through the hook package 05 owns in `internal/identity` (`RegisterUserRemover`, `RegisterOrgRemover` in `internal/identity/removers.go`; this package only registers, as package 39 does): this package exports `RemoveVarScope(tx, scope, scope id)` and `internal/hub` registers it for the user and the org scope, beside package 39's `RemoveScope`. One mechanism serves secrets and variables; this package registers no maintenance task.
17. **`parley vars list` and `parley vars resolve` print one document `{"items":[…]}`**, without `next_cursor`, after following `next_cursor` to the end with `limit=200`: the shape and paging of `parley secrets list` (package 39). The PRD says "all pages" for `list` and names no paging flag for either.
18. **`parley vars create` always prints the `results` document**, for one scope too, and prints `{"results":[]}` when every scope failed. With no scope flag the one scope is `user`.
19. **Malformed arguments** are: an entry without `=` when `--from-stdin` is not given; an empty key before `=`; an empty entry between commas; with `--from-stdin`, any number of arguments other than one, or an argument containing `=` or `,`; for `update`, more than one entry; a scope flag on `resolve`. The line ending dropped from standard input is one `\n` or one `\r\n`.
20. **`parley vars delete` prints the key as typed**, not the stored casing, because the route answers `204` with no body.
21. **Time comes from a replaceable clock**, so tests control `created_at` and `updated_at`.

## Glossary

- **Hub**: The `parleyd` server.
- **Workspace**: A repository the hub holds, identified by its `slug`. Either a registered repository or a task fork.
- **Task fork (fork)**: A workspace created from another workspace (its parent) for one task. It shares history with the parent, has its own branches and expires.
- **Scope / permission**: A string carried by a PAT that grants read or write access to an area. Not to be confused with the scope of an entry (`user`, `org`, `workspace`), which names its owner.
- **Bound token**: A PAT confined to one workspace (and the forks created with it).
- **Sandbox**: An isolated environment in which an agent runs, attached to a workspace (normally a task fork) and started with it checked out.
- **Exposed secret**: A secret that a profile names in `expose_secrets`. Its real value is placed in the sandbox's environment, where code in the sandbox can read it.
- **Credential (sandbox)**: A secret attached to a sandbox as an OpenShell provider. The workload sees only a placeholder.
- **Hub event**: A record of something the hub did (`parley.*` types), with a sequence number. Hub events form the audit log and the event stream.
- **Variable**: A named, readable value owned by a user, an organization or a workspace.
- **Resolution chain**: The ordered scopes a workspace's variables and secrets are looked up in: the workspace, its parent when it is a fork, its organization, its owner.
- **Reserved name**: One of the secret names the hub itself reads from a workspace's own scope for origin, upstream and forge webhook credentials.

# Requirements

## Requirements

### REQ-1: Access to variable routes by scope

**Rationale:** A variable is configuration of its owner, so each scope decides who may read it and who may change it, and a caller without access must learn nothing.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-1.1] IF a PAT calls a variable list route without `vars:read` and without `vars:write`, or calls a variable create, update or delete route without `vars:write`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request before deciding scope access, and change nothing
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `insufficient_scope`; the same answer for an existing and a nonexistent organization or workspace; a PAT with `vars:write` alone is served on the list routes; an API key and the admin token are served without any scope
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, a table over {route: each of the 12 variable routes} x {credential: PAT without vars scopes, PAT vars:read, PAT vars:write, API key}: assert status 403 and error_type insufficient_scope exactly where the criterion says, on slug w and on slug nosuch alike; assert PAT vars:write gets 200 on GET /user/vars; assert the API key is never answered insufficient_scope
   ```
1. [REQ-1.2] IF the admin token calls any route under `/user/vars`, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request
   → HTTP 403 with `error_type` `forbidden` and the message `user-scoped endpoints require a user credential`; nothing is stored, changed or deleted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_access_test.go, a table over POST /user/vars, GET /user/vars, PATCH /user/vars/A, DELETE /user/vars/A with the admin token: assert status 403; assert error_type == 'forbidden'; assert message == 'user-scoped endpoints require a user credential'; assert the variable table has no row of scope user
   ```
1. [REQ-1.3] WHEN a user calls a route under `/user/vars`, THE parleyd SHALL act on the variables whose scope is `user` and whose scope id is the caller's user id, and on no other user's
   → an entry U created is listed for U and absent from the list of every other user
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O

   in internal/secret/var_access_test.go: as U POST /user/vars {entries:[{key:'A',value:'1'}]}; assert GET /user/vars as U lists A; assert GET /user/vars as M lists nothing; assert PATCH /user/vars/A as M is 404 not_found
   ```
1. [REQ-1.4] IF a route under `/orgs/:slug/vars` names an organization that does not exist, or an organization of which the calling user is not a member, or one that is blocked, THEN THE parleyd SHALL answer as if the organization did not exist
   → HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found`; the response body for an existing organization the caller is not a member of is byte-for-byte the body for a nonexistent slug; nothing is stored, changed or deleted

   ```

   ```
1. [REQ-1.5] WHEN a member of the organization, or the admin token, calls a route under `/orgs/:slug/vars`, naming the organization by its slug or its UUID, THE parleyd SHALL act on the variables whose scope is `org` and whose scope id is that organization's id

### REQ-2: Creating variables

**Rationale:** Configuration is usually set several keys at a time, and a half-applied set is worse than none.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-2.1] WHEN a caller with write access to the scope posts `{"entries":[{"key","value"}, …]}` to `POST /user/vars`, `POST /orgs/:slug/vars` or `POST /workspaces/:slug/vars` and every check passes, THE parleyd SHALL store every entry with the key casing given, treat a missing `value` as the empty string, and answer the created entries in request order
   → HTTP 201 with `{"items":[{key, value, created_at, updated_at}, …]}` and no other member per item; every item has the same `created_at`, equal to its `updated_at`, in RFC 3339 UTC with whole seconds; a key of 255 characters, a value of exactly 262,144 bytes and an empty value are accepted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, for each of the three scopes: POST entries [{key:'Zed',value:'1'},{key:'alpha'},{key: 255 letters, value: 262144 bytes}] (the server body limit raised for the test); assert status 201; assert keys in request order with given casing; assert items[1].value == ''; assert every created_at == updated_at == the fixed clock's instant formatted with whole seconds; assert item members are exactly key, value, created_at, updated_at; assert GET lists the three
   ```
1. [REQ-2.2] IF the create body has no `entries`, an `entries` that is empty or not an array, an entry that is not an object, a key that is absent, not a string, empty, longer than 255 characters, starting with a digit or holding a character other than an ASCII letter, a digit or `_`, a value that is not a string or is longer than 262,144 bytes, or two keys equal ignoring case, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the whole request and store nothing
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; for a fault of one entry the message contains that entry's key; the scope's variables are unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_validate_test.go and internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, a table over the bodies {no entries, entries: [], entries: 'x', entries: [1], key absent, key: 7, key: '', key of 256 letters, key '1A', key 'A-B', key 'É', value: 5, value of 262145 bytes, value of 131073 two-byte characters, keys 'Foo' and 'FOO'} each beside one valid entry: assert status 400 and error_type invalid_request; assert the message contains the offending key where there is one; assert the list is still empty
   ```
1. [REQ-2.3] IF the number of variables already in the scope plus the number of entries in the request is more than 100, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the whole request, also when a key of the request already exists in the scope
   → HTTP 429 with `error_type` `secret_limit_reached` and the message `maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded`; nothing is stored; a request that brings the scope to exactly 100 is answered 201; secrets of the same scope and variables of other scopes are not counted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: seed 98 variables in W's scope and 100 in U's user scope; POST 2 new entries to /workspaces/w/vars -> 201 (count 100); POST 1 new entry -> 429, error_type secret_limit_reached, message == 'maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded'; POST 1 entry whose key already exists -> 429, not 409; assert count is still 100
   ```
1. [REQ-2.4] IF a key of the request is already present in the scope, compared ignoring case, and the scope is not full, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the whole request and store none of its entries
   → HTTP 409 with `error_type` `conflict` and the message `key "<k>" already exists`, where `<k>` is the key as given in the request; the other entries of the request are not stored and the existing entry is unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: with variable 'Token' = 'old' in the scope, POST entries [{key:'NEW',value:'1'},{key:'TOKEN',value:'2'}]; assert status 409, error_type conflict, message == 'key "TOKEN" already exists'; assert the list holds only Token = old
   ```
1. [REQ-2.5] THE parleyd SHALL for any create request with more than one fault, answer the fault that comes first in this order: `entries` not a non-empty array; an invalid key; an invalid value; two keys equal ignoring case; the scope's limit; a key already present
   → the status and `error_type` are those of the first failing check
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, a table over pairs of faults {invalid key + oversized value -> 400 naming the invalid key, oversized value + duplicate keys -> 400 naming the oversized entry's key, duplicate keys + full scope -> 400, full scope + existing key -> 429}: assert status, error_type and the key named
   ```
1. [REQ-2.6] THE parleyd SHALL for any two concurrent create requests on one scope that carry the same key ignoring case, store the key once
   → exactly one request is answered 201 and the other 409 `conflict`; the scope then holds one entry for the key, and none of the losing request's other entries
   Check: integration
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_store_test.go: start 2 goroutines posting [{key:'k'},{key:'a1'}] and [{key:'K'},{key:'a2'}] to /workspaces/w/vars, repeated 20 times on fresh scopes; assert the statuses are {201, 409}; assert the scope holds exactly 2 entries, both from the winning request
   ```
1. [REQ-2.7] WHEN a create is repeated with the same `Idempotency-Key`, caller, route and body within 24 hours of a successful create, THE parleyd SHALL create nothing and answer the original body

1. [REQ-2.8] WHILE no secret encryption key is configured, THE parleyd SHALL serve every variable route as when a key is configured

### REQ-3: Listing, updating and deleting variables

**Rationale:** A value that can be set must be readable, changeable and removable by the name a person remembers, whatever casing they type.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-3.1] WHEN a caller with read access to the scope calls `GET /user/vars`, `GET /orgs/:slug/vars` or `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars`, THE parleyd SHALL answer that scope's own variables with their values, ordered by key ascending ignoring case, in pages
   → HTTP 200 with `{"items":[{key, value, created_at, updated_at}, …],"next_cursor":…}`; `items` is an array also when empty; `limit` defaults to 50 and `next_cursor` is null on the last page; a fork's list never holds its parent's variables
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   - setup: a fork F of a workspace that holds a variable P
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go: seed keys 'b', 'A', 'c', 'B2' in W and 'P' in a parent of fork F; assert GET /workspaces/w/vars item keys == ['A','b','B2','c'] with values; assert GET with limit=2 then the cursor yields the same four once each and next_cursor null at the end; assert an empty scope answers items [] and next_cursor null; assert GET /workspaces/f/vars does not hold 'P'; seed 51 keys in U's scope and assert the first page holds 50
   ```
1. [REQ-3.2] WHEN a caller with write access to the scope sends `PATCH …/vars/:key` with `{"value": string}` and the key matches a variable of the scope ignoring case, THE parleyd SHALL replace the value, keep the stored key casing and `created_at`, and set `updated_at` to the current time
   → HTTP 200 with the entry `{key, value, created_at, updated_at}`; `key` is the stored casing; the empty string is accepted as a value; a value of exactly 262,144 bytes is accepted
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, for each scope: create 'ApiUrl' = 'a' at t0; advance the clock to t1; PATCH …/vars/APIURL {value:'b'}; assert status 200, key == 'ApiUrl', value == 'b', created_at == t0, updated_at == t1; PATCH {value:''} -> 200 and value == ''; assert GET lists the new value
   ```
1. [REQ-3.3] IF the body of a `PATCH …/vars/:key` has no `value`, a `value` that is `null` or not a string, or a value longer than 262,144 bytes, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request, whether or not the key exists, and leave the variable as it was
   → HTTP 400 with `error_type` `invalid_request`; the stored value and `updated_at` are unchanged
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, a table over the bodies {{}, {value:null}, {value:3}, {value: 262145 bytes}} on an existing key and on a missing key: assert status 400 and error_type invalid_request; assert the entry is unchanged
   ```
1. [REQ-3.4] IF a `PATCH …/vars/:key` with a valid body or a `DELETE …/vars/:key` names a key that matches no variable of the scope ignoring case, THEN THE parleyd SHALL refuse the request and change nothing
   → HTTP 404 with `error_type` `not_found` and the message `key "<k>" not found`, where `<k>` is the key as given in the path; a key that exists only in another scope, or only as a secret of the same scope, is not a match
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O

1. [REQ-3.5] WHEN a caller with write access to the scope sends `DELETE …/vars/:key` and the key matches a variable of the scope ignoring case, THE parleyd SHALL delete that variable

### REQ-4: Events for variable changes

**Rationale:** Every change to configuration must be visible afterwards to the people who can see the scope, without the record ever holding a value.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-4.1] WHEN a create of variables succeeds, THE parleyd SHALL write one `parley.variable.create` event per created entry, in request order, in the same transaction as the entries
   → each event has `resource_type` `variable`, `action` `create`, `resource_id` the stored key, the caller as actor, and `metadata` exactly `{"scope", "scope_id", "key"}` with scope `user`, `org` or `workspace` and scope id the user id, the organization id or the workspace slug; the event's `workspace` is the slug for the workspace scope and null for the other two
   Check: integration
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   - setup: the real event component writing to the store
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_events_test.go, a table over the three scopes: POST two entries; read the event log; assert two parley.variable.create events in request order; assert resource_type, action, resource_id, actor, metadata == {scope, scope_id, key} and workspace == 'w' or null as the criterion says
   ```
1. [REQ-4.2] WHEN an update of a variable succeeds, THE parleyd SHALL write one `parley.variable.update` event with the fields of a create event and `action` `update`, in the same transaction as the update
   → `resource_id` and `metadata.key` are the stored key casing, not the casing of the request path
   Check: integration
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O
   - setup: the real event component writing to the store
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_events_test.go: create 'ApiUrl' in o; PATCH /orgs/o/vars/APIURL; assert exactly one new event, type parley.variable.update, action update, resource_id == 'ApiUrl', metadata.key == 'ApiUrl', metadata.scope == 'org', metadata.scope_id == O's id, workspace == null
   ```
1. [REQ-4.3] WHEN a delete of a variable succeeds, THE parleyd SHALL write one `parley.variable.delete` event with the fields of a create event and `action` `delete`, in the same transaction as the delete

   → no member of a `parley.variable.*` event, its metadata included, equals or contains the value

   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O

1. [REQ-4.5] IF a create, update or delete of variables is refused with any error status, or a create is answered as an idempotent replay, THEN THE parleyd SHALL write no variable event

### REQ-5: The resolution chain of a workspace

**Rationale:** Variables and secrets must be looked up in one order that depends only on the workspace, so that every caller and every sandbox gets the same answer.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-5.1] WHEN the chain of a repository workspace is asked for, THE parleyd SHALL answer, highest priority first, the workspace's own `workspace` scope with origin `workspace`, the `org` scope of its organization with origin `org`, and the `user` scope of its owner with origin `user`
   → an ordered list of steps, each with origin, scope and scope id; no step has origin `parent`
   Check: unit

   ```

   → four steps in that order; the user step is the user who created the fork, not the parent's owner
   Check: unit

   → the chain has no step with origin `org`; for a fork whose owner left the organization the parent step is still present

### REQ-6: Resolved variables of a workspace

**Rationale:** An agent configures itself from the values its workspace or fork runs with, and needs to know where each one came from.

   → HTTP 200 with `{"items":[{key, value, origin, created_at, updated_at}, …],"next_cursor":…}`; each key occurs once ignoring case; key casing, value and both timestamps are those of the winning entry; `origin` is `workspace`, `parent`, `org` or `user`; `limit` and `cursor` page the list as on every list
   Check: unit
   - setup: a test hub on the real router with a real store in t.TempDir(), a fixed clock, a user U with an API key, an organization O (slug o) with U as member, a user M who is a member of O, a user X who is a member of nothing, and a repository workspace W (slug w) owned by U in O

   ```
1. [REQ-6.2] WHEN the workspace named is a task fork, THE parleyd SHALL include the parent workspace's variables with origin `parent`, below the fork's own and above the organization's

### REQ-7: Secrets by name along the chain

**Rationale:** A sandbox gets its credentials and exposed secrets from the workspace it is attached to, and a fork of a read-only contributor must never receive what belongs to the parent.

   → per name: found with `value` and `origin` (`workspace`, `parent`, `org` or `user`), or missing; beside them the list of scopes searched, in chain order, each with origin, scope and scope id; an empty list of names answers no entries and no error; a secret whose value is the empty string is found
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real store with workspace records written through the record store of internal/access, users and organizations through internal/identity: user U owns repository workspace W in organization O and is a member of O; user M is a member of O and owns fork F of W; U owns fork G of W

1. [REQ-7.2] WHILE the workspace is a task fork whose owner has write access to the parent workspace, THE parleyd SHALL search the parent's `workspace` scope as the second step for every name that is not a reserved name

### REQ-8: Removal of variables with their owner

**Rationale:** Configuration must not outlive what it configures, and a slug that is used again must not inherit the values of the workspace that had it before.

#### Criteria

1. [REQ-8.1] WHEN the removal of a workspace or of a task fork runs this package's remover with its transaction and the slug, THE parleyd SHALL delete every variable whose scope is `workspace` and whose scope id is that slug, inside that transaction, and write no variable event
   → after the transaction commits the slug has no variables; variables of other workspaces, of the parent, of users and of organizations are untouched; the remover returns no revoked token ids and the event log gains no `parley.variable.*` event
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_remove_test.go: tx = store.Begin(); remove(tx, 'f'); tx.Commit(); assert count(workspace, 'f') == 0, count(workspace, 'w') == 3, count(user, U) == 2, count(org, O) == 2; assert no parley.variable event was written
   ```
1. [REQ-8.2] IF the transaction the remover ran in is rolled back, or the remover's delete fails, THEN THE parleyd SHALL leave every variable of the slug in place, and return the failure to the caller of the remover
   → after a rollback the slug's variables are listed as before; a failing delete returns a non-nil error, so that the removal's transaction is rolled back
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables
   ```
   in internal/secret/var_remove_test.go: tx = store.Begin(); remove(tx, 'w'); tx.Rollback(); assert count(workspace, 'w') == 3 and the values are unchanged; call remove with a transaction that is already closed and assert err != nil
   ```
1. [REQ-8.3] WHEN a workspace is created under a slug whose earlier workspace was removed, THE parleyd SHALL start the new workspace with no variables
   → `GET /workspaces/:slug/vars` answers an empty `items`, and the resolved set holds no entry with `origin` `workspace`
   Check: integration
   - setup: a real store; a workspace W (slug w) with 3 variables, a fork F (slug f) of W with 2 variables, a user U with 2 user-scope variables, an organization O with 2 org-scope variables

   ```

### REQ-9: The parley vars commands

**Rationale:** People and scripts set configuration from a shell, often for several scopes at once.

#### Criteria

[REQ-9.2] WHEN `parley vars create` is run with one or more of `--user`, `--org <slug>` and `--workspace <slug>`, or with none, THE parley CLI SHALL send one create per scope given, in the order user, org, workspace whatever the order of the flags, to `/user/vars`, `/orgs/<slug>/vars` and `/workspaces/<slug>/vars`, and send only the user request when no flag is given

## Execution Paths

### PATH-1: A developer sets values at two levels and reads what the workspace runs with

1. **developer** posts LOG_LEVEL=info to /orgs/:slug/vars and log_level=debug to /workspaces/:slug/vars
2. **parleyd** checks scope and access, stores both entries and writes one parley.variable.create event for each
3. **developer** reads GET /workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved
4. **parleyd** builds the workspace's chain, merges the scopes and answers log_level = debug with origin workspace
5. **developer** deletes /workspaces/:slug/vars/LOG_LEVEL and reads the resolved set again
6. **parleyd** deletes the workspace's entry, writes parley.variable.delete and answers LOG_LEVEL = info with origin org

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** HTTP router and check pipeline, authentication, scope check, workspace access rule, variable routes, variable store, resolution chain, event component, store

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a real store
- a user with an API key who is a member of an organization and owns a workspace record in it

**End state:**

- the last resolved read holds one entry: key LOG_LEVEL, value info, origin org
- the event log holds two parley.variable.create events and one parley.variable.delete event, none carrying a value
- GET /workspaces/:slug/vars answers an empty items array

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/vars_test.go: post('/orgs/o/vars', {entries:[{key:'LOG_LEVEL',value:'info'}]}) == 201; post('/workspaces/w/vars', {entries:[{key:'log_level',value:'debug'}]}) == 201; r = get('/workspaces/w/vars/resolved'); assert r.items == [{key:'log_level', value:'debug', origin:'workspace', …}]; delete('/workspaces/w/vars/LOG_LEVEL') == 204; r = get('/workspaces/w/vars/resolved'); assert r.items[0].key == 'LOG_LEVEL' and origin == 'org'; assert the types in the event log
```

### PATH-2: An org member's fork runs with the parent's variables and without its secrets

1. **developer** stores the variable REGION and the secret DEPLOY_KEY on a workspace the developer owns
2. **org member** reads GET /workspaces/:fork/vars/resolved on a task fork of that workspace that the org member owns
3. **parleyd** builds the fork's chain with the parent step and answers REGION with origin parent
4. **parleyd** resolves the secret DEPLOY_KEY for the member's fork: the fork's owner has no write access to the parent, so the parent's scope is skipped and the name is missing
5. **parleyd** resolves the same name for a fork the developer owns and finds it with origin parent

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** variable routes, variable store, resolution chain, secret resolution, secret store with a test encryption key, workspace access rule, identity memberships, store

**Setup:**

- a test hub on the real router with a real store and a test encryption key
- a developer owning workspace w in organization o; an org member of o owning fork f of w; a fork g of w owned by the developer; fork records written through the record store of internal/access

**End state:**

- the member's resolved read of f holds REGION with origin parent
- secret resolution for f answers DEPLOY_KEY missing and lists the scopes searched without the parent's
- secret resolution for g answers DEPLOY_KEY with the stored value and origin parent

**Pseudocode:**

```
in internal/secret/resolve_integration_test.go: as developer post('/workspaces/w/vars', REGION=eu) and post('/workspaces/w/secrets', DEPLOY_KEY=s3) (or store the secret through the secret store); as member r = get('/workspaces/f/vars/resolved'); assert r holds {REGION, 'eu', parent}; a = resolveSecrets('f', ['DEPLOY_KEY']); assert a missing and a.searched origins == [workspace, org, user]; b = resolveSecrets('g', ['DEPLOY_KEY']); assert b value == 's3' and origin == 'parent'
```

### PATH-3: A developer manages variables from the shell

1. **developer** runs `parley vars create A=1,B=x=y --user --workspace <slug>`
2. **parley CLI** sends POST /user/vars and then POST /workspaces/<slug>/vars with both entries
3. **parleyd** stores the entries in both scopes and answers 201 twice
4. **parley CLI** prints one results document with the user and the workspace scope and exits 0
5. **developer** runs `parley vars resolve <slug>`
6. **parley CLI** reads GET /workspaces/<slug>/vars/resolved to the last page and prints the entries with their origin

**Smoke check — real components (must not be mocked):** parley CLI command tree and HTTP client, HTTP router and check pipeline, variable routes, variable store, resolution chain, store

**Setup:**

- a hub started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a real store
- a user with an API key who owns a workspace record; the CLI run through cli.Run with the hub's URL and that key

**End state:**

- the create prints results for the scopes user and workspace, each with A and B, and exits 0
- the resolve prints items A = 1 and B = x=y, both with origin workspace, and exits 0
- `parley vars list --user` prints A and B from the user scope

**Pseudocode:**

```
in test/e2e/vars_test.go: code, out, _ = parley('vars','create','A=1,B=x=y','--user','--workspace','w'); assert code == 0 and scopes(out.results) == ['user','workspace']; code, out, _ = parley('vars','resolve','w'); assert code == 0; assert out.items == [{key:'A',value:'1',origin:'workspace',…},{key:'B',value:'x=y',origin:'workspace',…}]; code, out, _ = parley('vars','list','--user'); assert keys(out.items) == ['A','B']
```

# Tasks

## Test Commands

- **all_tests:** `go test ./... -count=1`
- **linter:** `golangci-lint run ./...`
- **spec_tests:** `go test ./internal/secret/... ./internal/cli/... ./test/e2e/... -count=1`

## Dependencies

- `39` — reads secrets by scope and name through its store for name resolution, and shares internal/secret
- `09` — builds parley vars on its HTTP client, command helper, output and exit-code rules
- `52` — writes parley.variable.create, update and delete through its event component in the transaction of the change
- `14` — registers the removal of a workspace's variables with the removers of owned data that the workspace delete runs
- `16` — registers the same removal with the removal participants of a fork's removal
- `05` — registers its variable removal with RegisterUserRemover and RegisterOrgRemover, the scope removers it owns in internal/identity/removers.go

### 1. Create variables in the user, org and workspace scopes (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-2

**Steps:**

- 1.1 Add the behaviours of this task to internal/secret/var_validate_test.go, internal/secret/var_store_test.go and internal/secret/var_routes_test.go, with a test hub helper that mounts the routes on the real router with a real store, a fixed clock, users, an organization and a workspace record, and confirm they fail
- 1.2 Write the key and value rules: a key is 1 to 255 ASCII letters, digits and underscores and does not start with a digit; a value is a string of at most 262,144 bytes counted in bytes; a missing value is the empty string; members of the wrong type are invalid
- 1.3 Register a schema migration with internal/store for a variable table keyed by scope, scope id and the lower-cased key, holding the key as given, the value, created_at and updated_at, so that the store refuses a second entry for a key ignoring case
- 1.4 Build the store's create operation: in one transaction count the scope's variables, refuse when the count plus the new entries is over 100, refuse when a key is present ignoring case, else insert every entry with one timestamp from the clock; a failure leaves nothing stored
- 1.5 Build the part that turns a request into a scope and a scope id: the caller's user id for /user/vars (the admin token refused with 403 forbidden and the message `user-scoped endpoints require a user credential`), the organization found with the organization selector of internal/identity (a slug or a UUID) for /orgs/:slug/vars (members of the active organization and the admin token; anyone else and an unknown organization 404 not_found with one body), answering as the scope resolvers of package 39's secret routes do, and the workspace for /workspaces/:slug/vars through the access component of internal/access with need write
- 1.6 Register POST /user/vars, POST /orgs/:slug/vars and POST /workspaces/:slug/vars through internal/server as creates that accept Idempotency-Key, needing the scope vars:write for a PAT; the user and org routes are declared as naming no workspace, the workspace route as naming :slug
- 1.7 Run the body checks in the fixed order (entries a non-empty array; each key valid; each value valid; no two keys equal ignoring case; the limit; no key present) and answer the first fault: 400 invalid_request naming the key, 429 secret_limit_reached with the message `maximum of 100 entries per scope exceeded`, or 409 conflict with the message `key "<k>" already exists`
- 1.8 Answer 201 with items of key, value, created_at and updated_at in request order, timestamps in RFC 3339 UTC with whole seconds
- 1.9 Make the routes independent of the secret encryption key: they answer the same with and without one

### 4. Build the resolution chain and answer a workspace's resolved variables (implement)

### 6. Resolve secrets by name along the chain (implement)

**Criteria:** REQ-7

**Depends on:** 4

- 6.2 Read secrets through package 39's Get(scope, scope id, name), which answers (value, found, error) and an error matching ErrUnreadable for an entry that cannot be decrypted; take that one method as the resolution's reader so the tests can wrap it, and define no second read operation
- 6.3 Build the exported resolution function: given a slug and a list of names, build the chain at that call and, for each distinct name in the order first asked, read the scopes in chain order and stop at the first that has the name; answer per name found with value and origin, or missing, and beside them the scopes searched in order
- 6.4 For a fork, ask the access component whether the fork's owner has write access to the parent; when not, drop the parent step for every name before any read, so the parent's scope is never read and is not among the scopes searched

- 6.6 Treat a secret with an empty value as found

- 6.8 Return the workspace-not-found error for an unknown slug and a different error for a store failure; keep no value, chain or access answer between calls and write no value to a log
- 6.9 Export the function from internal/secret so that the sandbox packages can call it, and pass its collaborators in internal/hub

- 8.3 Add the scope flags --user, --org <slug> and --workspace <slug> to create, list, update and delete; no flag means the user scope; list, update and delete refuse more than one with a usage error; resolve takes no scope flag
- 8.4 Parse entries: split arguments at commas, split each entry at its first `=`, refuse an entry without `=`, an empty key and an empty entry; with --from-stdin take exactly one bare key and read the value from the command's standard input, dropping one trailing `\n` or `\r\n`; every refusal is a usage error raised before any request
- 8.5 create: send one POST per scope in the order user, org, workspace; collect each success as {scope, items}; print each failed scope's envelope once on stderr and go on; print the one results document, also when it is empty; exit 1 when any scope failed, else 0
- 8.6 list: read the scope's list with limit=200, follow next_cursor to the end, and print {"items":[…]} without next_cursor, as parley secrets list does; a hub error on any page prints nothing on stdout
- 8.7 update: accept exactly one entry, send PATCH with the value to the key's path through the shared client so the key is percent-encoded as one segment, and print the entry
- 8.8 delete: send DELETE to the key's path and print {"deleted": <the key as typed>}
- 8.9 resolve: take one workspace slug, read the resolved list with limit=200 to the last page and print {"items":[…]} without next_cursor
- 8.10 Add test/e2e/vars_test.go with the two end-to-end flows of this package that run against a hub started in-process

**Touches:**

- `internal/cli/vars.go`
- `internal/cli/vars_test.go`
- `internal/cli/root.go`
- `test/e2e/vars_test.go`
